When multilingual tool calls fail, is the binding bottleneck language understanding/action selection, or satisfying a language-conditioned execution interface after the action is already understood?

data.source: ATR frontier-map（问题，不是论文结论）
explanations: Language affects semantic grounding and tool/argument selection upstream.
Language mainly conflicts with an otherwise fixed execution convention downstream.
data.freshness: Refresh on a direct multilingual function-calling diagnostic or any new contract-aware benchmark.

nodes.label: Are multilingual reliability losses determined by a language's structural role (instruction, content, response/value, schema), rather than by a coarse 'non-English' setting label?

data.source: ATR frontier-map（问题，不是论文结论）
explanations: A single cross-lingual gap aggregates essentially similar language mismatches.
Different language roles produce distinct mechanisms and cannot be collapsed into one gap.
data.freshness: Refresh when a fully crossed function-calling study or benchmark revision appears.

nodes.label: When a strict multilingual function-call score falls, what evidence permits attribution to agent action capability rather than to the benchmark's translation, gold-value, or undocumented interface policy?

data.freshness: Refresh after any item-level provenance audit, native-language calibration, or contract-aware ranking result.

nodes.label: Do output constraints improve syntactic validity while changing the semantic or language correctness of multilingual argument values, and under what explicitly declared interface convention?

data.source: ATR frontier-map（问题，不是论文结论）
explanations: Constrained decoding is principally a syntax fix and should not materially affect semantic values.
Constraint systems can redirect value generation, creating legal but semantically or conventionally wrong calls.
data.freshness: Refresh on direct multilingual constrained-decoding/function-calling evidence.

nodes.label: When tool-schema wording changes function-calling behavior, is the operative variable the natural language of the schema, or the instruction signal and semantic quality carried by schema text?

data.source: ATR frontier-map（问题，不是论文结论）
explanations: Matching the schema language to the user language is the principal multilingual intervention.
Schema language alone matters little once semantic content/wording is controlled; wording and representation are the operative intervention.
data.freshness: Refresh on a multilingual schema-quality/function-calling study or a benchmark release with controlled schema variants.

nodes.label: Can intrinsic tokenizer disparity predict a distinct multilingual tool-action failure before evaluation, or is it only a broad correlate of resource, pretraining coverage, and generic downstream performance?

data.source: ATR frontier-map（问题，不是论文结论）
explanations: Tokenizer fragmentation has a condition-specific predictive relationship with a declared function-call error locus.
Any apparent tokenization-action association is explained by resource/pretraining coverage or is no more informative than existing general tokenizer-performance associations.
data.freshness: Refresh on a direct tokenization-plus-multilingual-function-calling study, or after a public asset establishes a declared argument-value contract.

nodes.label: When a multilingual capability is claimed to transfer through model merging, does the experiment compose two independently learned compatible components, or only interpolate a base checkpoint with its own task-SFT derivative?

data.source: ATR frontier-map（问题，不是论文结论）
explanations: A distinct language/CPT component and task/alignment component can be composed, making capability-transfer attribution testable.
An apparent merge effect is ordinary retention, dilution, or interference of one task-SFT delta because no separate language component exists.
data.freshness: Refresh on a new multilingual model-merging result or a revision-pinned compatible component pair.

nodes.label: A tool call may have the right intent and selected tool while violating an execution convention in an argument value; separately, protocol implementers have needed to converge schema-validation behavior across clients and servers.

data.incumbent_practice: Treat structured-tool validation and a strict multilingual score as an adequate proxy for correct action.
data.material_consequence: Without a declared value and validator contract, an evaluator or platform owner cannot tell whether a strict failure should be repaired as semantic action, interface realization, or validation interoperability.
data.candidate_construct: an explicit, inspectable action contract that separates semantic intent, executable value convention, and validator interpretation
alternative_explanations: The observed multilingual error is mainly upstream semantic grounding, so a contract layer adds little explanatory value.
The error is mainly a language-conditioned value/interface mismatch after action selection, and its interpretation depends on an unexposed contract.
data.does_not_establish: Neither signal establishes a benchmark-wide defect, a deployment-harm estimate, or a generally effective contract intervention.
